item.research_question: How do varying WC contents (10, 20, and 30 wt.%) affect the microstructure, mechanical properties, and wear resistance of FeCoCrNi high entropy alloy matrix composites prepared by spark plasma sintering?
item.material_system: FeCoCrNi matrix with WC particle reinforcements (10 wt.%, 20 wt.%, 30 wt.% WC)
item.processing_route: Two-step ball milling (10 h at 300 rpm with anhydrous ethanol as process control agent) followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1000 °C for 15 min under 30 MPa pressure
item.test_conditions: Room temperature compression testing; reciprocating dry friction and wear tests using a GCr15 steel ball, 5 N load, 3 Hz frequency, and 20 min duration
key_findings: The microhardness of the 30 WC–HEA composite reached 459.2 HV, which is 71.2% higher than the 268.3 HV of the pure matrix material.
The compressive yield strength of the 30 WC–HEA composite reached 1315.1 MPa, which is 112.1% higher than that of the pure matrix material.
The compression deformation rate of the 30 WC–HEA composite significantly decreased to 16.6% compared to over 40% for the pure matrix.
The average friction coefficient decreased from 0.68 for the pure matrix to 0.55 for the 20 WC–HEA composite before rising to 0.60 for the 30 WC–HEA composite.
The wear volume of the 30 WC–HEA composite was 1.47 × 10^5 μm^3, accounting for only 3.17% of the pure matrix material's wear volume (4.63 × 10^6 μm^3).
The sintered composites were mainly composed of an FCC matrix phase (Ni, Fe) and carbide phases including Cr7C3, Co3W3C, and WC.
The densification of the samples gradually decreased with the increase of WC content, ranging from 99.1% for the pure matrix to 97.1% for the 30 WC–HEA composite.
item.mechanism: The improvement in hardness and strength is attributed to second phase strengthening by hard WC and carbide phases, dislocation strengthening from thermal expansion mismatch, fine grain strengthening, and solid solution strengthening from dissolved W and C atoms. The wear resistance improvement is due to the high hardness and deformation resistance of WC particles, which shift the wear mechanism from adhesive wear in the pure matrix to abrasive wear in the composites, while the formation of Cr-rich and Co3W3C carbides further reduces wear volume.
item.limitations: Excessive WC addition (30 wt.%) leads to a sharp decrease in plasticity and brittle fracture, and causes the formation of excessive Cr-rich phases that create interface problems and slightly increase the friction coefficient.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work; however, it notes that research on particle-reinforced HEA matrix composites is still in its infancy and that the reinforcement particles have excellent anti-wear performance, suggesting further exploration of WC-reinforced systems.
quotes: The hardness of the 30 WC–HEA composites was the highest at 459.2 HV, which is 71.2% higher than the 268.3 HV of the pure matrix material.
The wear volume of 30 WC–HEA was the lowest, only 3.17% of that of the pure matrix material.
The compression deformation rate of the 30 WC–HEA composite significantly decreased to 16.6%.
